project_type: MCP server (TypeScript, Node 22) — a superset of Playwright MCP with a local Laya on-device decision engine
build_system: pnpm + tsc. Scripts: build (tsc), typecheck (tsc --noEmit), test (vitest run), start (node dist/index.js). bin: laya-browser-mcp -> dist/index.js
test_framework: vitest. Offline tests use a stubbed Laya (implements the SystemOne decision interface) and local static HTML fixtures served from disk (file:// or an in-process http server). Real-weights test is gated behind LAYA_MODEL_DIR env and skipped when absent.
verification_instructions: 1) pnpm install  2) pnpm exec playwright install chromium  3) pnpm run typecheck  4) pnpm run build  5) pnpm run test (offline, stubbed Laya + HTML fixtures)  6) optional: node dist/index.js then send an MCP initialize/list-tools over stdio to confirm the server boots and advertises tools.
snapshot_or_generated_files: None checked in. The Laya ONNX bundle (~1.7GB, 5 files: laya.onnx, laya.onnx.data, laya_config.json, tokenizer/tokenizer.json, tokenizer/tokenizer_config.json) is NOT committed; it is downloaded/exported at runtime and cached under ~/.cache/receptron-laya (LAYA_CACHE) or pointed to via modelDir/LAYA_MODEL_DIR.
setup_instructions: corepack enable && pnpm install; pnpm exec playwright install chromium. Node 22 default via nvm. Python 3.11+ via pyenv/uv only needed IF running the optional ONNX export spike for the web-agent checkpoint.
environment_constraints: Network: OPEN_INTERNET. Chromium must be installed via 'playwright install chromium' (was NOT preinstalled at the default 1.63 path during routing; installer works). The ~1.7GB Laya weights download and the Python torch export are heavy; the product and its test suite MUST run fully WITHOUT weights (Assist mode standalone + Autopilot degrades gracefully + stubbed Laya in tests). The web-agent ONNX-export spike is time-boxed and its outcome does not block delivery.
contribution_requirements: Project license MIT. Laya weights Apache-2.0 (Convai Innovations). Any Mind2Web-derived material CC BY 4.0 (attribute Deng et al., NeurIPS 2023; do not redistribute the test set). Positioning must stay honest: fast local decision layer + LLM fallback; strong on structured forms, weak on arbitrary real sites (web-agent v3: ~97.7% per-step on clean synthetic forms, ~1 step in 5 fully right on real Mind2Web sites). Do NOT market as a fully autonomous general web agent.
key_patterns: VERIFIED: @receptron/laya@0.1.2 API is `const laya = await Laya.load({ modelDir, repo, subfolder, revision, cacheDir, executionProviders, sessionOptions })` then `const r = await laya.systemOne(state, questions)`. questions = keyed object of { type: 'choice'|'score'|'noul', instructions, criteria } where choice/score criteria carry the options; answers at r.answers.<key>.choice/.probabilities/.score/.noul and r.usage.input_tokens. Limits: options must fit head_max_len (192 tok) — throws otherwise; <~20 options per choice recommended; state truncated to max_len (512 English checkpoint / 2048 web-agent). Deps: onnxruntime-node, @huggingface/tokenizers. VERIFIED: Playwright MCP tool convention is `element` (human-readable desc, optional) + `target` (exact ref like e5 from snapshot, or a unique selector). VERIFIED (important): stable playwright-core 1.63.0 does NOT expose `_snapshotForAI`/`snapshotForAI` (only alpha/mcp-bundled builds). Therefore DO NOT depend on that private API. Instead OWN the ref boundary: inject an in-page DOM walk that assigns stable `data-laya-ref="eN"` attributes to interactive/landmark elements and returns (a) a compact human-readable snapshot with [ref=eN] markers and (b) a ref->metadata map; Assist tools resolve a target ref via `page.locator('[data-laya-ref="eN"]')`, falling back to treating target as a raw selector. VERIFIED: web-agent (abedinia/laya-web-agent) is mmBERT-base 322M, jev_ultrafast I/O format (goal + title + visible text + numbered controls with current values + recent actions -> operation in {CLICK,TYPE_TEXT,SELECT,SCROLL_DOWN,WAIT,DONE,BLOCKED} + target=numbered control), max_len 2048/head_max_len 512. AUTHORITATIVE DESIGN LESSON (laya-ultrafast): Laya answers NARROW questions reliably but NOT the open 'what next?'; the working policy = narrow Laya decisions + deterministic rules (fill goal-stated values; after typing/opening a control choose from options that appeared; submit then open named item) + ONE text-model plan per task; a DONE decision is not proof of success, verify the final page independently.
relevant_files: src/types.ts — core data shapes: PageState, Control, DecisionQuestion, DecisionResult, LayaDecisionEngine interface (design FIRST)
src/snapshot.ts — in-page DOM walk assigning data-laya-ref; produces snapshot text + ref map
src/browser.ts — Playwright lifecycle + ref resolution boundary
src/state-builder.ts — AX/DOM snapshot -> compact typed PageState for Laya
src/laya/stub.ts — deterministic fake engine for tests
src/autopilot/loop.ts — snapshot->state->decision->execute->repeat; DONE/BLOCKED; confidence + MCP-sampling escalation; deterministic rules
src/server.ts / src/index.ts — MCP server (stdio) registering Assist tools + laya_run_goal
test/fixtures/*.html — local structured-form fixtures for offline Autopilot tests
directory_structure: Greenfield at repo root /projects/sandbox/laya-browser (git initialized, branch main, no commits). Everything is created fresh: src/ (server, tools, snapshot, state-builder, laya engine+stub, autopilot loop, types), test/ (vitest + HTML fixtures), docs/PLAN.md, README.md, package.json, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts.
